text:
Mia: FYI nightly eval popped a weird regression on the billing-assistant promptset — failure rate jumped ~7x vs baseline. Samples show completions that look like they came from other tenants (prefix bleed).
eval-bot: nightly-eval: billing-assistant: 7/120 failures (regression delta +6.3%). First detected 2024-08-03 05:12 UTC. Attachments: failing_examples.zip
Sam: omg. any repro IDs? is this deterministic or flakey across reruns?
Mia: put a couple example inputs in the zip. rerun of the failing seed gives different answers sometimes — non-deterministic. logs hint at cache hits when they shouldn't.
Akshay: this smells like a cache key normalization mismatch between quantized runtime and main runtime. saw similar in a local fuzz awhile back where trailing whitespace got dropped for certain quant kernels.
Julia: can you paste the offending keys from the cache log? also which model variant was used in the nightly run?
Mia: model = rwd/gptq-4x-8bit:v2 (rolled out to nightly yesterday). logs show keys like:
```
cached_key: tenantA|phash:3a5f|prefix:"user: pay\n"
cached_key: tenantB|phash:3a5f|prefix:"user: pay"  <-- missing trailing newline
=> normalized storage id: kvid:0x9f3b12  (collision)
```
Sam: oh that explains it — two different logical prefixes mapping to the same kv id. if the quant path trims/normalizes whitespace for alignment, you get cross-tenant collisions when prefix hash isn't salted with tenant id or when normalization differs.
Akshay: confirming: our prefix-cache key = sha256(tenant_id + prompt_hash + normalized_prefix) where normalized_prefix used to be exact bytes. a change in the quant kernel's tokenization/pack routine introduced whitespace stripping for alignment, and the cache key formation step for that code path didn't include the same normalization. so different code paths generate different 'normalized_prefix' but the storage lookup uses the stripped form.
Julia: regression start time matches the quant rollout. mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: disable prefix cache for gptq variants in nightly; 2) add tenant salt to storage id; 3) unify normalization in both runtimes.
Mia: can we flip a flag for the nightly job? want to stop noisy failures while we fix proper patch.
Akshay: quick toggle is available. curl to admin to flip:
```
curl -X PATCH "https://console.internal/admin/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"disable_prefix_cache_for_models": ["rwd/gptq-4x-8bit:v2"]}'
```
Sam: +1 do that, and run a focused nightly rerun to confirm false positives go away.
Julia: I'll open a GH issue and assign. filing now: rwd/infra#3421 - "kv key normalization mismatch for quantized runtime causing cross-tenant prefix collisions". adding logs and failing examples.
Mia: thanks — flipping flag now and re-running evals. will post results.
Sam: :eyes:
eval-bot: nightly-eval rerun queued (triggered by @Mia).
